verses.zh: 耶和华留下这几族，为要试验那不曾知道与迦南争战之事的以色列人，
verses.en: These were the nations the Lord permitted to remain so he could use them to test Israel—he wanted to test all those who had not experienced battle against the Canaanites.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “did not know the wars of Canaan.”

verses.zh: 好叫以色列的后代又知道又学习未曾晓得的战事。
verses.en: He left those nations simply because he wanted to teach the subsequent generations of Israelites, who had not experienced the earlier battles, how to conduct holy war.[NOTE:1]
notes: The Hebrew syntax of v. 2 is difficult. The Hebrew text reads literally, “only in order that the generations of the Israelites might know, to teach them war—only those who formerly did not know them.”sn The stated purpose for leaving the nations (to teach the subsequent generations…how to conduct holy war) seems to contradict 2:22 and 3:4, which indicate the nations were left to test Israel’s loyalty to the Lord. However, the two stated purposes can be harmonized. The willingness of later generations to learn and engage in holy war would measure their allegiance to the Lord (see B. G. Webb, Judges [JSOTSup], 114-15).

verses.zh: 所留下的就是非利士的五个首领和一切迦南人、西顿人，并住黎巴嫩山的希未人，从巴力・黑们山直到哈马口。
verses.en: These were the nations:[NOTE:1] the five lords of the Philistines, all the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites living in Mount Lebanon, from Mount Baal Hermon to Lebo Hamath.[NOTE:2]
notes: The words “These were the nations,” though not present in the Hebrew text, are supplied in the translation for clarity.
Or “the entrance to Hamath.”

verses.zh: 留下这几族，为要试验以色列人，知道他们肯听从耶和华藉摩西吩咐他们列祖的诫命不肯。
verses.en: They were left to test Israel, so the Lord would know if his people would obey the commands he gave their ancestors through Moses.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “to know if they would hear the commands of the Lord which he commanded their fathers by the hand of Moses.”

verses.zh: 以色列人竟住在迦南人、赫人、亚摩利人、比利洗人、希未人、耶布斯人中间，
verses.en: The Israelites lived among the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.

verses.zh: 娶他们的女儿为妻，将自己的女儿嫁给他们的儿子，并事奉他们的神。
verses.en: They took the Canaanites’ daughters as wives and gave their daughters to the Canaanites;[NOTE:1] they worshiped[NOTE:2] their gods as well.
notes: Heb “to their sons.”
Or “served”; or “followed” (this term occurs in the following verse as well).

verses.zh: 以色列人行耶和华眼中看为恶的事，忘记耶和华―他们的　神，去事奉诸巴力和亚舍拉，
verses.en: The Israelites did evil in the Lord’s sight.[NOTE:1] They forgot the Lord their God and worshiped the Baals and the Asherahs.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “in the eyes of the Lord.”
The Asherahs were local manifestations of the Canaanite goddess Asherah.

verses.zh: 所以耶和华的怒气向以色列人发作，就把他们交在美索不达米亚王古珊・利萨田的手中。以色列人服事古珊・利萨田八年。
verses.en: The Lord was furious with Israel[NOTE:1] and turned them over to[NOTE:2] King Cushan Rishathaim[NOTE:3] of Armon Haraim.[NOTE:4] They were Cushan Rishathaim’s subjects[NOTE:5] for eight years.
notes: Or “The Lord’s anger burned (or raged) against Israel.”
Heb “sold them into the hands of.”
Or “Cushan the Doubly Wicked.”

Armon Haraim. Traditionally Aram-Naharaim, and sometimes understood as a place in Mesopotamia. This reading accepts the consonantal text but divides the words after the nun (נ) instead of before. The consonants ארמן הרים could be read with a dual ending as ʾArmon Haraim, meaning “Citadel of the Two Mountains,” or with a plural ending as ʾArmon Harim, meaning “Citadel of the Mountains.” In either case, Cushan Rishathaim is probably a remaining Canaanite king with a fortress in the hill country of Israel. See Beitzel, The Moody Atlas of Bible Lands, 106.
Or “they served Cushan Rishathaim.”

verses.zh: 以色列人呼求耶和华的时候，耶和华就为他们兴起一位拯救者救他们，就是迦勒兄弟基纳斯的儿子俄陀聂。
verses.en: When the Israelites cried out for help to the Lord, he[NOTE:1] raised up a deliverer for the Israelites who rescued[NOTE:2] them. His name was Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb’s younger brother.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “the Lord.”
Or “delivered.”
“Caleb’s younger brother” may refer to Othniel or to Kenaz (in which case Othniel is Caleb’s nephew).

verses.zh: 耶和华的灵降在他身上，他就作了以色列的士师，出去争战。耶和华将美索不达米亚王古珊・利萨田交在他手中，他便胜了古珊・利萨田。
verses.en: The Lord’s Spirit empowered him[NOTE:1] and he led Israel. When he went to do battle, the Lord handed over to him King Cushan Rishathaim of Armon,[NOTE:2] and Othniel overpowered him.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “was on him.”
Armon. Traditionally Aram. See note at Judges 3:8. This is either Armon, with restored nun (נ), being short for Armon Haraim, or perhaps the entire phrase was original.
Heb “his hand was strong against Cushan Rishathaim.”

verses.zh: 于是国中太平四十年。基纳斯的儿子俄陀聂死了。
verses.en: The land had rest for 40 years; then Othniel son of Kenaz died.

verses.zh: 以色列人又行耶和华眼中看为恶的事，耶和华就使摩押王伊矶伦强盛，攻击以色列人。
verses.en: The Israelites again did evil in the Lord’s sight.[NOTE:1] The Lord gave King Eglon of Moab control over Israel[NOTE:2] because they had done evil in the Lord’s sight.
notes: Heb “in the eyes of the Lord” (also later in this verse).
Heb “strengthened Eglon…against Israel.”

verses.zh: 伊矶伦招聚亚扪人和亚玛力人，去攻打以色列人，占据棕树城。
verses.en: Eglon formed alliances with[NOTE:1] the Ammonites and Amalekites. He came and defeated Israel, and they seized the city of date palm trees.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and he gathered to him.”
The city of date palm trees refers to Jericho. See Deut 34:3.

verses.zh: 于是以色列人服事摩押王伊矶伦十八年。
verses.en: The Israelites were subject to[NOTE:1] King Eglon of Moab for 18 years.
notes: Or “the Israelites served Eglon.”

verses.zh: 以色列人呼求耶和华的时候，耶和华就为他们兴起一位拯救者，就是便雅悯人基拉的儿子以笏；他是左手便利的。以色列人托他送礼物给摩押王伊矶伦。
verses.en: When the Israelites cried out for help to the Lord, he[NOTE:1] raised up a deliverer for them. His name was Ehud son of Gera the Benjaminite, a left-handed man.[NOTE:2] The Israelites sent him to King Eglon of Moab with their tribute payment.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “the Lord.” This has been replaced by the pronoun (“he”) in the translation for stylistic reasons.

The phrase, which refers to Ehud, literally reads “bound/restricted in the right hand,” apparently a Hebrew idiom for a left-handed person. See Judg 20:16, where 700 Benjaminites are described in this way. Perhaps the Benjaminites purposely trained several of their young men to be left-handed warriors by restricting the use of the right hand from an early age so the left hand would become dominant. Left-handed men would have a distinct military advantage, especially when attacking city gates. See B. Halpern, “The Assassination of Eglon: The First Locked-Room Murder Mystery,” BRev 4 (1988): 35.
Heb “The Israelites sent by his hand an offering to Eglon, king of Moab.”

verses.zh: 以笏打了一把两刃的剑，长一肘，带在右腿上衣服里面。
verses.en: Ehud made himself a sword—it had two edges and was 18 inches long.[NOTE:1] He strapped it under his coat on his right thigh.
notes: The Hebrew term גֹּמֶד (gomed) denotes a unit of linear measure, perhaps a cubit (the distance between the elbow and the tip of the middle finger—approximately 18 inches [45 cm]). Some suggest it is equivalent to the short cubit (the distance between the elbow and the knuckles of the clenched fist—approximately 13 inches [33 cm]) or to the span (the distance between the end of the thumb and the end of the little finger in a spread hand—approximately 9 inches [23 cm]). See BDB 167 s.v.; HALOT 196 s.v.; B. Lindars, Judges 1-5, 142.

verses.zh: 他将礼物献给摩押王伊矶伦（原来伊矶伦极其肥胖）；
verses.en: He brought the tribute payment to King Eglon of Moab. (Now Eglon was a very fat man.)

verses.zh: 以笏献完礼物，便将抬礼物的人打发走了，
verses.en: After Ehud brought the tribute payment, he dismissed the people who had carried it.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “the tribute payment.”

verses.zh: 自己却从靠近吉甲凿石之地回来，说：「王啊，我有一件机密事奏告你。」王说：「回避吧！」于是左右侍立的人都退去了。
verses.en: But he went back[NOTE:1] once he reached[NOTE:2] the carved images[NOTE:3] at Gilgal. He said to Eglon,[NOTE:4] “I have a secret message for you, O king.” Eglon[NOTE:5] said, “Be quiet!”[NOTE:6] All his attendants left.
notes: Or “returned” (i.e., to Eglon’s palace).
The words “once he reached” are supplied in the translation for clarification. The Hebrew text simply reads “from.”
Or “idols.”
The words “to Eglon” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
Heb “he”; the referent (Eglon) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Or “Hush!”

verses.zh: 以笏来到王面前；王独自一人坐在凉楼上。以笏说：「我奉　神的命报告你一件事。」王就从座位上站起来。
verses.en: When Ehud approached him, he was sitting in his well-ventilated[NOTE:1] upper room all by himself. Ehud said, “I have a message from God[NOTE:2] for you.” When Eglon rose up from his seat,[NOTE:3]
notes: Or “cool.” This probably refers to a room with latticed windows which allowed the breeze to pass through. See B. Lindars, Judges 1-5, 144.
Heb “word of [i.e., from] God.”
Or “throne.”

verses.zh: 以笏便伸左手，从右腿上拔出剑来，刺入王的肚腹，
verses.en: Ehud reached with his left hand, pulled the sword from his right thigh, and drove it into Eglon’s[NOTE:1] belly.
notes: Heb “his”; the referent (Eglon) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 连剑把都刺进去了。剑被肥肉夹住，他没有从王的肚腹拔出来，且穿通了后身。
verses.en: The handle went in after the blade, and the fat closed around the blade, for Ehud[NOTE:1] did not pull the sword out of his belly.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Ehud) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

The Hebrew text has “and he went out to the [?].” The word פַּרְשְׁדֹנָה (parshedonah) occurs only here, and is of uncertain meaning. The noun has the directional suffix, meaning “to the parshedon.” Some translations (e.g. KJV, NRSV, NASB, ESV, NKJV) take it as a reference to feces or intestinal organs coming out. This would interpret the noun ending as feminine (not directional). But the verb (וַיֵּצֵא, vayyetseʾ) is masculine so this does not explain the text, even though the notion might fit the context. The subject is either Ehud or the blade–either would match the verb form–and the word in question tells where the subject went out. If the blade (לַהַב, lahav) is the subject, then פַּרְשְׁדֹנָה (parshedonah) might be an anatomical reference describing the exit point; if Ehud is the subject, then the word is probably a technical architectural term. The entire phrase is missing from the LXX. The present translation omits the clause, understanding it as an ancient variant of the first clause in v. 23. See B. Lindars, Judges 1-5, 146-48, for discussion of the options.

verses.zh: 以笏就出到游廊，将楼门尽都关锁。
verses.en: As Ehud went out into the vestibule,[NOTE:1] he closed the doors of the upper room behind him and locked them.
notes: Again the precise meaning of the Hebrew word, used only here in the OT, is uncertain. Since it is preceded by the verb “went out” and the next clause refers to Ehud closing doors, the noun is probably an architectural term referring to the room (perhaps a vestibule; see HALOT 604 s.v. מִסְדְּרוֹן) immediately outside the king’s upper chamber. As v. 24 indicates, this vestibule separated the upper room from an outer room where the king’s servants were waiting.

verses.zh: 以笏出来之后，王的仆人到了，看见楼门关锁，就说：「他必是在楼上大解。」
verses.en: When Ehud had left, Eglon’s[NOTE:1] servants came and saw the locked doors of the upper room. They said, “He must be relieving himself[NOTE:2] in the well-ventilated inner room.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “his.”
Heb “covering his feet” (i.e., with his outer garments while he relieves himself).
The Hebrew expression translated “well-ventilated inner room” may refer to the upper room itself or to a bathroom attached to or within it.

verses.zh: 他们等烦了，见仍不开楼门，就拿钥匙开了，不料，他们的主人已死，倒在地上。
verses.en: They waited so long they were embarrassed, but he still did not open the doors of the upper room. Finally they took the key and opened the doors.[NOTE:1] Right before their eyes was their master, sprawled out dead on the floor![NOTE:2]
notes: The words “the doors” are supplied.
Heb “See, their master, fallen to the ground, dead.”

verses.zh: 他们耽延的时候，以笏就逃跑了，经过凿石之地，逃到西伊拉；
verses.en: Now Ehud had escaped while they were delaying. When he passed the carved images, he escaped to Seirah.

verses.zh: 到了，就在以法莲山地吹角。以色列人随着他下了山地，他在前头引路，
verses.en: When he reached Seirah,[NOTE:1] he blew a trumpet[NOTE:2] in the Ephraimite hill country. The Israelites went down with him from the hill country, with Ehud in the lead.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “When he arrived.”
That is, “mustered an army.”
Heb “now he was before them.”

verses.zh: 对他们说：「你们随我来，因为耶和华已经把你们的仇敌摩押人交在你们手中。」于是他们跟着他下去，把守约旦河的渡口，不容摩押一人过去。
verses.en: He said to them, “Follow me, for the Lord is about to defeat your enemies, the Moabites!”[NOTE:1] They followed him, captured the fords of the Jordan River[NOTE:2] opposite Moab,[NOTE:3] and did not let anyone cross.
notes: Heb “for the Lord has given your enemies, Moab, into your hand.” The verb form (a Hebrew perfect, indicating completed action from the standpoint of the speaker) emphasizes the certainty of the event. Though it had not yet taken place, the Lord speaks of it as a “done deal.”
The word “River” is not in the Hebrew text, but is supplied for clarity.
Or “against Moab,” that is, so as to prevent the Moabites from crossing.

verses.zh: 那时击杀了摩押人约有一万，都是强壮的勇士，没有一人逃脱。
verses.en: That day they killed about 10,000 Moabites[NOTE:1]—all strong, capable warriors; not one escaped.
notes: Heb “They struck Moab that day—about ten thousand men.”

verses.zh: 这样，摩押就被以色列人制伏了。国中太平八十年。
verses.en: Israel humiliated Moab that day, and the land had rest for 80 years.

verses.zh: 以笏之后，有亚拿的儿子珊迦，他用赶牛的棍子打死六百非利士人。他也救了以色列人。
verses.en: After Ehud[NOTE:1] came[NOTE:2] Shamgar son of Anath. He killed 600 Philistines with an oxgoad. So he also delivered Israel.
notes: Heb “him”; the referent (Ehud) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “was.”
